question: What public-domain condition applies to a new traffic control device proposed for experimentation or interim approval?
model_answer: Direct Answer: A new traffic control device is not eligible for official experimentation or interim approval unless it is in the public domain, meaning all forms of proprietary protection (patents, trademarks, copyrights) have been expressly abandoned. For experimentation, the agency, manufacturer/developer, and supplier must all provide a legally-binding certification of public-domain status, acknowledging that any future proprietary protection will result in removal from the MUTCD or cancellation of the approval or authorization. Standards (mandatory): - "A traffic control device design or application shall not be eligible for official experimentation (see Section 1B.05) or interim approval (see Section 1B.07) unless it is in the public domain. Express abandonment of any and all forms of proprietary protection, such as patents, trademarks, or copyrights, related to the design and application of the traffic control device shall satisfy the requirement for the traffic control device to be in the public domain." - A request for experimentation involving a new device or new application "shall include from the agency conducting the experiment, the manufacturer and/or developer of the device, and the supplier of the device, a legally-binding statement certifying that the traffic control device is not protected by a patent, trademark, or copyright in accordance with Section 1D.06, and that the traffic control device is in the public domain and can be used freely in traffic control device design and application without infringement or claim of trade secret misappropriation." - "The legally-binding statement shall also state that the agency conducting the experiment, the manufacturer and/or developer of the device, and the supplier of the device are aware that if patent, trademark, or copyright protection is established in the future for the device or application, such action will result in its removal from the MUTCD, cancellation of its interim approval, or cancellation of the authorization for experimentation." - The request for permission to experiment shall contain, among other items, "a legally-binding statement that the experimental device or application is in the public domain, in accordance with Paragraph 16 of this Section." Citations: - Section 1D.06 Standard §2 (p.34) - Section 1B.05 Standard §16 (p.9) - Section 1B.05 Standard §10 (p.8)
gold_answer: The traffic-control message, design, or application must be in the public domain and not protected by patent, trademark, or copyright. Legally binding statements are required from the relevant agency/developer/supplier for experimentation. Protection of internal components or manufacturing methods can still be allowed.
